A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same KnowShiftQA study. Text and rendered-page inspection covered all 13 pages, including figures, tables, and Appendices A–H, without comparison-limiting gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, question-answering, and knowledge-shift experiments in Tables 2–4, plus detailed results and prompting comparisons in Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The hypothetical knowledge-update procedure, dataset curation pipeline, retrieval approaches, and Locate-and-Answer prompting remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices B, C, and G.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five subjects, five question types, textbook sources, and hypothetical knowledge-shift scenarios. No dataset, task, or domain coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 and 8–10 retain identical retrieval, LLM, RAG-system, and prompting comparators. The newly cited AutoSchemaKG work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Paragraph-level retrieval, recall@1/5, zero-shot QA accuracy, reranking with k = 6, and prompting protocols are unchanged. No experimental setting or evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The knowledge-shift comparison in Table 4, subject/type analyses in Appendix F, and direct-answer versus Locate-and-Answer comparison in Appendix G are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Experimental values and findings in Tables 2–4 and 8–10 are identical, including Table 4's 22.47–26.92 percentage-point accuracy drops under hypothetical knowledge updates. Dataset and curation statistics also match.

T1.justification: Question-type definitions and reasoning patterns are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contribution and claims about RAG fragility under knowledge shifts and difficulties integrating contextual and parametric knowledge.

C2.justification: Results interpretations, the Limitations section, and Appendix H's discussion of calibration and instruction following are identical. Applicability boundaries and omitted retrieval paradigms remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Curation details, model descriptions, prompting instructions, dataset statistics, textbook licenses, and the code-access link remain unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Bai et al. (2025a), AutoSchemaKG, to the existing discussion of structured-data RAG, with a corresponding reference entry. The previously cited neural graph database paper remains, relabeled 2025b; research positioning otherwise matches.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to the arXiv version/date stamp and citation disambiguation accompanying the added reference. Prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citation changes line wrapping in Section 4 and reflows bibliography entries across pages 6–8. All figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds one reference to an existing related-work statement, with minor editorial and layout adjustments. The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations—including Appendices A–H—remain unchanged, so the bibliographic addition does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
